evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We ran a cluster RCT of weekly SMS adherence reminders for adults on ART at 8 NGO-supported clinics in Kisumu County, Kenya. 1,640 patients, 12 months. Viral suppression at 12 months was 9 percentage points higher in the SMS arm (95% CI 3 to 15), pre-registered primary outcome. The NGO's own adherence counselors sent the messages from a dashboard, phoned anyone who replied 'need help' within 24 hours, and had caseloads of about 120. Cost was about USD 4.10 per patient per year including counselor time. The county health department wants to roll it out to all 71 ART clinics (about 48,000 patients) run by county staff, with messages sent automatically from the national EMR and no dedicated counselor to answer replies, because the budget allows USD 1.50 per patient. The decision is a county budget line for next fiscal year; the county says it can drop it after a year if it fails. Subgroup results: the effect was concentrated in patients enrolled under 12 months; near zero in patients stable on ART for more than 3 years. Will this hold at scale?
evals.expected_output: A scalability assessment in the output template that marks all seven rows, gives one of the three verdicts, and names one test to run first under county delivery.
assertions: Fills all seven rows of the pilot-against-scale table, each marked plus, minus, or more information needed.
Marks the dropped call-back to 'need help' replies as a minus.
Notes that the effect sat in newly enrolled patients and that the scale population differs.
Gives 'Promising: test first' or 'Does not yet merit scale-up', not 'Recommended for scale-up'.
Names one first test run by the county under routine conditions, with a comparison group.
Does not project an at-scale effect size or add up a total score.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our pilot worked. Can we scale it?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the pilot's result, how it was delivered, and the proposed scale-up, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the pilot's result: the effect, its comparison, and the design.
Asks who delivered the pilot and with what support.
Asks who would deliver at scale and what would change.
Gives no verdict and no table.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our NGO ran immunization camps with small in-kind incentives in 60 villages in Udaipur district, Rajasthan, with our own nurses and village mobilizers. Full immunization by 24 months rose from 22% to 41% in the camp-plus-incentive villages, in a randomized evaluation we pre-registered. The state health department now wants to adopt the model statewide through its own ANMs and ASHAs, as a permanent line in the state budget starting next year, covering roughly 33 districts and 2 million children. Once it is in the budget and the ANMs' job descriptions, the department says it will not revisit it. Please assess whether the effect will survive.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces the assessment, marks the change from NGO staff to government health workers as untested, and tells the user to bring in a specialist because the decision cannot be reversed.
assertions: Marks the row on who delivers as a minus because the move from NGO nurses to ANMs and ASHAs was not tested.
Names a first test under state delivery in a few sites before the permanent budget line.
Tells the user to consult an evaluator or implementation researcher together with the state's planners.
Says what to bring to them.
Does not quote the 19-point gain as the expected statewide effect.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our scalability assessment for the Kisumu SMS program came back 'promising, test first', and the county agreed to a 10-clinic test of county-run reply handling. Now write the roll-out plan: who does what in which quarter across the 71 clinics, how we hand the dashboard to the county, and how it gets financed after the donor leaves.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the assessment is done and the request is for a scale-up strategy, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the request is for how to reach routine delivery, not whether the effect will survive.
Does not produce a pilot-against-scale table or a roll-out plan.
